text.content: At Cascadia, most support requests move through a predictable series of steps — classify the message, look up the order, check the warranty, draft a response. Each step depends on the one before it. Sofia knows she does not need agents talking to each other on the fly for this. She needs a sequential workflow: one step finishes, then the next begins, using the output of the previous step.

Summary

text.content: Sequential orchestration is the natural pattern when tasks have clear dependencies. It is predictable, easy to debug, and easy to extend one step at a time — but it is also the slowest when steps could otherwise happen in parallel. In the next lesson, we look at hierarchical orchestration, where a coordinator sits above the specialists rather than in a line with them.
